graduate_admissions.q: How do I apply to a graduate program at CSULB?
graduate_admissions.a: Submit your application through Cal State Apply (calstate.edu/apply). Pay the $70 nonrefundable fee. Then complete any program-specific supplemental applications.
No. CSULB does not offer application fee waivers for graduate applicants. The fee is $70.

Submit official transcripts electronically or by mail to Enrollment Services. Master's applicants need transcripts from their bachelor's institution and most recent school. Doctoral applicants also need master's transcripts. Email: ES-IDPTrans@csulb.edu

graduate_admissions.q: What GPA do I need for graduate admission?
graduate_admissions.a: Minimum 2.5 cumulative GPA OR minimum 2.5 in last 60 semester (90 quarter) units. Programs may require higher. GPA is NOT rounded.

graduate_admissions.q: How do I check my application status?
graduate_admissions.a: Log into MyCSULB. Admissions reviews for minimum eligibility, then forwards qualified candidates to academic departments.

graduate_admissions.q: Can I appeal an admission decision?
graduate_admissions.a: Appeals are rarely successful. Must include new, serious, and compelling information submitted within 15 days of the admission decision.

international_students.q: Can international students apply to CSULB graduate programs?
international_students.a: Yes. International students should contact the Center for International Education (CIE) for transcript standards, English requirements, and visa guidance.

international_students.q: How do international students submit transcripts?
Can international students transfer credit units?
international_students.a: Up to 30% of required units may be transferred from international institutions.

graduate_center_services.q: How do I book an appointment with the Graduate Center?
graduate_center_services.a: Current CSULB students: BeachConnect student portal. Prospective students (including alumni and community members): YouCanBookMe calendar.

graduate_center_services.q: What services does the Graduate Center offer?
graduate_center_services.a: Application advising, statement of purpose review, CV/resume review, writing support, workshops, GradMentor, Grad Slam, mental health intern consultations, statistical consulting.

graduate_center_services.q: Does the Graduate Center provide program advising?
graduate_center_services.a: No. Contact your department's graduate advisor for course registration, scheduling, and graduation requirements.

academic_support.q: Where can I get tutoring as a graduate student?
academic_support.a: The Learning Center, University Writing Center, Lindgren Math Tutoring Center, college-specific tutoring (Business, Engineering), and the Graduate Center for writing.

academic_support.q: What are CSULB's AI guidelines for graduate students?

research_and_scholarly.q: How can I present my research?
research_and_scholarly.a: Student Research Competition (Feb 27, 2026), Week of RSCA, Grad Slam (3-minute video, cash prizes), and CSU-Wide Grad Slam.

research_and_scholarly.q: How do I find funding to attend a conference?
research_and_scholarly.a: Apply for the Graduate Travel Fellowship (up to $1,000), ASI Student Travel Fund, or SLD Travel Grant (up to $400).

culminating_activities.a: Departmental and college approval of your planned course of study. Required before your culminating activity (thesis/dissertation/exam).

culminating_activities.q: What is the culminating activity for a master's degree?
culminating_activities.a: Varies by program: thesis, project, and/or comprehensive exam. Check with your graduate advisor and the University Catalog.

culminating_activities.q: When is the thesis/dissertation submission deadline for Spring 2026?
culminating_activities.a: Master's thesis/project signature page: February 23 – April 7, 2026 (paper date: May 2026). Doctoral dissertation: May 11, 2026. Departmental deadlines may be earlier.

graduation.q: How do I apply to graduate?
graduation.a: Submit your graduation application through MyCSULB Student Records: https://www.csulb.edu/student-records/apply-to-graduate-graduate-students

graduation.q: How long does degree clearing take?
graduation.a: Approximately 4–8 weeks after the semester ends.

campus_resources.q: How do I register for classes?
campus_resources.a: Register through MyCSULB Student Center after consulting your advisor and the Schedule of Classes. Watch for your registration appointment email each term.

campus_resources.q: How do I get a student ID?
campus_resources.a: Obtain your Beach ID from ID Card Services at the Beach Shops / University Bookstore.

campus_resources.q: Is on-campus housing available for graduate students?
campus_resources.a: Three residential colleges exist (Beachside, Hillside, Parkside) but housing is not guaranteed. Most graduate students live off-campus. Contact housing@csulb.edu or (562) 985-4187.

campus_resources.q: How do I get a bus pass?
campus_resources.a: Long Beach Transit U-PASS TAP Card is available via Parking and Transportation Services.

financial_aid.q: How do I apply for financial aid as a graduate student?
financial_aid.a: Complete the FAFSA or California Dream Act (CADA) application, then check the Financial Aid portal: https://www.csulb.edu/financial-aid-and-scholarships/how-to-apply-for-aid-graduate-students

financial_aid.q: What scholarships are available for graduate students?
financial_aid.a: State University Grant (need-based), Graduate Equity Fellowship (faculty-nominated), Sally Casanova Pre-Doctoral Scholars ($5,000 stipend), and external scholarships via the Financial Aid Office.
Yes, through the Basic Needs Program: https://www.csulb.edu/student-affairs/basic-needs/financial

health_and_wellbeing.q: How do I access mental health counseling at CSULB?
health_and_wellbeing.a: Contact CAPS for an initial consultation: https://www.csulb.edu/student-affairs/counseling-and-psychological-services/initial-consultation. Crisis intervention: https://www.csulb.edu/student-affairs/counseling-and-psychological-services/crisis-intervention

health_and_wellbeing.q: How do I request disability accommodations?
health_and_wellbeing.a: Contact the Bob Murphy Access Center (BMAC): bmac@csulb.edu | (562) 985-5401 | SSSC building, Suite 110.
